sources.title: KIP-98: Exactly Once Delivery and Transactional Messaging
KIP-500: Replace ZooKeeper with a Self-Managed Metadata Quorum
KIP-848: The Next Generation of the Consumer Group Protocol

corrections: Updated Java Producer defaults: idempotence defaults to enabled when configurations do not conflict since Kafka 3.0, and linger.ms changed from 0ms to 5ms in Kafka 4.0.
Clarified that idempotence deduplicates producer retries but not application-level resends, and that Kafka EOS requires transactions, atomic offset commits, and read_committed consumers.

Corrected ISR membership to the time-based replica.lag.time.max.ms rule without a fixed message-lag threshold, and qualified high-watermark visibility with Last Stable Offset for read_committed consumers.
Removed reliance on a specific ISR member ordering during leader election and documented the availability-versus-data-loss tradeoff of unclean election.
Distinguished classic eager, cooperative, and Kafka 4.0 GA consumer rebalance protocols instead of describing every rebalance as a global stop-the-world event.
Updated KRaft lifecycle: Kafka 3.3 production readiness, ZooKeeper removal in Kafka 4.0, majority quorum availability, and Kafka 4.1 dynamic controller quorum support.
Qualified controller outages: existing data traffic may continue, while metadata changes and partition failure recovery depend on controller availability.
Replaced unsourced fixed throughput comparisons with workload-dependent qualitative descriptions and corrected Redis Streams replay support.

relationSuggestions.reason: The storage model is physically realized through partition logs, leaders, followers, and ISR replication.
acks=all and min.insync.replicas derive their durability semantics from ISR replication.
Group membership, assignment, and rebalance determine a subscribed consumer's partition ownership.
Idempotent and transactional producer features are necessary components of Kafka-scoped EOS.
Atomic offset submission and read_committed isolation complete the Kafka consume-process-produce EOS boundary.
KRaft applies a Raft-inspired replicated quorum log to Kafka cluster metadata, while retaining Kafka-specific protocol details.
